newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on Wall Street slide.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on Wall Street slide.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Sunday amid Wall Street's decline on Friday and expectations of rising inflation, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 1.62 percent, or 5.04 points, to 306.52 on a low all-share turnover of 139 million shekels against 240 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.49 percent lower at 312.03.

"The market was reacting today to Wall Street's decline on Friday. It was also affected by expectations of higher inflation in the next three months," said Michael Politzer, head of the economics department at the Central Securities Corp.
The Dow Jones Industrials slid 157 points on Friday in the ninth-largest decline in terms of points in the blue-chip average's history.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices. July's CPI, to published on August 15, is also feared to be a high one percent, some traders have said.

"Rising inflation might lead to higher interest rates and this will have a negative impact on the market. The fact that the Treasury proposes an inflation target (for 1998) of 7.0-10 percent instead of 6.0-9.0 percent (recommended by the Bank of Israel) is also seen as a negative development which might also lead to rising interest rates," Politzer said.
The Treasury has proposed to leave unchanged the 1998 inflation target at 7.0-10 percent. The Bank of Israel is pressing for the target to be lowered to 6.0-9.0 percent in 1998.

A trader at Bank Hapoalim said that despite today's fall, the market is expected to continue rising. "The market made a very big move and there are enough reasons for a technical correction. Despite this, it seems that the positive momentum will continue," he said.
"Wall Street's decline and inflation fears were a trigger for today's decline but the market is only looking for a reason to continue rising," the trader said.
"Even if the market continues to decline a day or two I am sure that it will resume its rise soon. The market is extremely strong and new money keeps coming in," Politzer said.
Elco Holdings, fell 1.5 percent to 2,892 agorot (Israeli cents). The company reported on Sunday second quarter earnings per share of 4.06 shekels against 3.77 shekels a year earlier.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which lost 0.25 percent to 834 agorot on turnover of 6.2 million shekels; Industrial Buildings, which gained 2.0 percent to 726 agorot on turnover of six million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 2.75 percent to 37,380 agorot on volume of 5.6 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
